//: UX-98: markdown correctness, not markdown opinions.
Enabled is the class that changes how a document *renders*. Disabled
is the class that argues about house style - this repository's docs
style is its own, and rule-by-rule fights with an opinionated default
are how a docs linter gets switched off six weeks later.
Table cell counts are NOT covered here and are checked by
implements MD001-MD048, and the table rules (MD055 pipe style, MD056
column count) are markdownlint v0.34+ additions with no PyMarkdown
equivalent. That was measured against the real defects, not assumed.
UX-109: the lint used to run without `-r`, so it scanned two files and
read as though it scanned `docs/`. Made recursive, which surfaced 1300
violations across ~150 documents. 1287 were fixed - they are the class
that changes rendering: blank lines around headings, lists and fences,
and fence languages. The 13 that remain are four rules arguing with
correct content, disabled below with a reason each, which is the same
trade every other disable here records.

front-matter.//: UX-240: .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md open with YAML frontmatter; without this the leading `---` reads as a setext heading and every skill fails MD022. No document under docs/ uses frontmatter, so nothing else changes.

md001.//: UX-109: heading increment - the imported spec numbers milestones `# M1` then `### Goal`; editing a contract document's headings for a linter is the wrong trade

md003.//: heading style: setext vs atx, pure preference

md004.//: unordered list marker style, pure preference

md012.//: multiple blank lines are used deliberately as section breaks

md013.//: line length: this repo wraps prose by meaning, not by column

md024.//: duplicate headings are correct in per-round audit files

md025.//: a second H1 is used to separate an appended resolution

md026.//: trailing punctuation in headings is deliberate here

md029.//: ordered list numbering style, pure preference

md033.//: inline HTML: the docs-style opt-out markers are HTML comments

md034.//: bare URLs are readable in plain text, which matters for terminal output

md036.//: bold-as-heading is used for inline emphasis in tables

md011.//: UX-109: reversed-link detection fires on a Python subscript - `compute_structural_metrics()['max_depth']` is not a link

md014.//: UX-109: `$`-prefixed commands - the one block it flags shows each command's timing on the same line, so the rule's premise (no output) is false there

md038.//: UX-109: spaces in a code span - both instances quote a literal whose trailing space is part of what is being described, and trimming it would falsify the quote

md041.//: first line need not be a heading in an appended fragment

md044.//: proper-name capitalisation needs a word list nobody will maintain

md046.//: code block style: fenced and indented both appear deliberately
